purpose: Representative empirical corpus for ScrollLibrary Standard Text quality qualification. These are test briefs, not canned manuscript outputs.

samples.title: Why Complex Systems Fail Slowly Before They Fail Suddenly
samples.brief: Explain hidden accumulation, feedback loops, normalization of deviance, resilience, leading indicators and recovery in complex systems for an educated general reader. Use concrete cross-domain examples but avoid pretending illustrative examples are empirical facts.
qualityPressures: clear distinction between example and evidence

samples.title: Pricing Power in the Age of AI
samples.brief: A practical but rigorous book for founders explaining pricing power, willingness to pay, switching costs, marginal cost, value metrics, bundling and AI-era product economics. Material market, legal or quantitative claims must be traceable to current sources.

samples.title: How Administrative States Learn
samples.brief: Compare how public institutions across different periods learned from crises, built administrative capacity and sometimes institutionalized failure. Keep chronology, actors and causal claims precise. Do not invent quotations or historical details.

samples.title: Reliable AI Agents in Production
samples.brief: Teach experienced developers how to design reliable production AI agents: budgets, termination conditions, tool contracts, idempotency, queues, retries, evaluation, observability, sandboxing and human escalation. Include useful code that is internally consistent and suitable for technical audit.

samples.title: The Invisible Decisions That Shape a Life
samples.brief: Narrative non-fiction about path dependence, small choices and delayed consequences. Use a strong human voice, recurring motifs and concrete scenes without fabricating real people, quotations or factual anecdotes. The manuscript should feel authored rather than templated.
